newsitem.title: UK: Bulgaria back in doldrums in slow Brady market.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria back in doldrums in slow Brady market.

text.p: Volatile Bulgarian Bradys dropped on Wednesday in a generally steady market that seemed to have little reason to head much higher for the moment, traders said.
Bulgaria's political and economic situation remains so precarious that its payment of a Brady coupon on Tuesday was far from enough to give more than modest support to prices.
"If that was the only issue, I would have bought it yesterday (when prices fell on rumours that payment was delayed)," one European bank trader said.
"But I'm looking at other things there...I think it will get worse," he added.
The ruling Socialists are so far refusing to budge on opposition calls for an early election and quick moves to sort out the country's economic chaos.
Anti-government protests are now in their 24th day.
Bulgarian IABs fell 3/8 of a point to 48-1/4.
Elsewhere, Russia was struggling to hold up.
Brazil started stronger on news that Congress had approved a bill that would allow President Fernando Henrique Cardoso to run for a second term.
But prices later fell back to New York's closing levels.

"Markets elsewhere are looking a bit dodgy. We might continue to outperform, but there isn't really a lot of reason to take prices higher," one trader said, pointing to uncertainty over the next direction of U.S. Treasuries.
